simple.meaning: הָגָה (hâgâh) is a Hebrew concept word meaning “to murmur (in pleasure or anger); by implication, to ponder.” BibleIQ follows how Scripture develops this idea across its occurrences.
simple.biblicalBackground: The concept appears 25 times across Joshua, Job, Psalms, Proverbs, Isaiah, and 1 more, beginning at Joshua 1:8. Its contexts include righteousness, Torah.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to הָגָה (H1897).
simple.whyItMatters: Concept words shape biblical themes. BibleIQ keeps the concept grounded in actual verse evidence instead of starting with a later theological definition.
simple.summary: הָגָה (hâgâh) / H1897 is traced through Joshua 1:8, Job 27:4, Psalms 1:2, Psalms 2:1 as a generated source-based concept entry.

structuredEvidence.definition: to murmur (in pleasure or anger); by implication, to ponder

firstOccurrence.englishText: This book of the law shall not depart from your mouth, but you shall meditate on it day and night, that you may observe to do according to all that is written in it; for then you shall make your way prosperous, and then you shall have good success.

majorEvents.evidenceText: For your hands are defiled with blood,

timeline.evidenceText: This book of the law shall not depart from your mouth, but you shall meditate on it day and night, that you may observe to do according to all that is written in it; for then you shall make your way prosperous, and then you shall have good success.
surely my lips will not speak unrighteousness,
but his delight is in Yahweh’s* “Yahweh” is God’s proper Name, sometimes rendered “LORD” (all caps) in other translations. law.
Why do the nations rage,
My tongue shall talk about your righteousness and about your praise all day long.
The mouth of the righteous talks of wisdom.
But I, as a deaf man, don’t hear.
For you have been my help.
My tongue will also talk about your righteousness all day long,
Your way, God, is in the sanctuary.
They have hands, but they don’t feel.
I remember the days of old.
For my mouth speaks truth.
The heart of the righteous weighs answers,
for their hearts plot violence

When they tell you, “Consult with those who have familiar spirits and with the wizards, who chirp and who mutter,” shouldn’t a people consult with their God? Should they consult the dead on behalf of the living?
Therefore Moab will wail for Moab. Everyone will wail. You will mourn for the raisin cakes of Kir Hareseth, utterly stricken.
For Yahweh says to me,
Your heart will meditate on the terror.
I chattered like a swallow or a crane.

definitions.short: to murmur (in pleasure or anger); by implication, to ponder
definitions.usage: imagine, meditate, mourn, mutter, roar, × sore, speak, study, talk, utter.
definitions.full: H1897. hagah I. הָגָה verb moan, growl, utter, speak, muse (only poetry) (onomatopoetic; Late Hebrew הָגָה muse, speak, spell a word, so Aramaic הֲגָא ; muse , especially Ethpa`al; Arabic satirize, insult, scold , also spell (borrowed meaning)) — Qal Perf. 2masculine singular וְהָגִ֫יתָ consecutive Josh 1:8 ; 1 singular הָגִ֫יתִי Psa 143:5 , וְהָגִיתִי consecutive 77:13 ; Imperfect יֶהְגֶּה Job 27:4 8 t.; 3 feminine singular תֶּהְגֶּה Psa 35:28 2 t., אֶהְגֶּה 63:7 ; Isa 38:14 , יֶהְגּוּ Psa 2:1 + 2t., תֶּהְגּוּ Isa 16:7 ; נֶהְגֶּה֑ 59:11 ; Infinitive absolute הָגוֺ 59:11 ; — 1 of inarticulate sounds : a. growl , of lion growling over prey, followed by על Isa 31:4 . b. groan, moan , in distress (like dove), absolute, Isa 38:14 ; 59:11 ( נֶהְגֶּה הָגוֺ ); sigh for ( לְ ) in sorrow, mourning, moan for 16:7 (|| לְ יְיֵלִיל ), so also Jer 48:31 . 2 utter , followed by accusative of thing, Psa 38:13 ; subject לָשׁוֺן Job 27:4 (|| דִּבֶּר ) Psa 35:28 ; 71:24 ; Isa 59:3 ; subject מֶּה Psa 37:30 ; Prov 8:7 — compare also below Po. below; speak (absolute) Psa 115:7 ( בְּ instrumental) 3. a. (soliloquize) meditate, muse , with בְּ of thing, Josh 1:8 ; Psa 1:2 ; 63:7 ; 77:13 ; 143:5 ; with accusative Isa 33:18 , subject לֵב . b. imagine, devise , with accusative Psa 2:1 ; Prov 24:2 (subject לֵב ); with Infinitive 15:28 (subject id. ) Po. Infinitive absolute only דִּבְרֵישֶֿׁקֶר מִלֵּב וְהֹגוֺ הֹרוֺ Isa 59:13 a conceiving and an uttering, out of the heart, lying words (|| וְסָרָה עשֶׁק דַּבֵּר ); — on form compare Kö i. 555 ; but read rather וְהָגוֺ הָרוֺ Qal Infinitive absolute compare Di; Ba NB 77 retains ᵑ0 & explanation as Qal Infinitive passive Hiph`il Participle plural וְהַמַּהְגִּ֥ים הַמְּצַפְצְפִים Isa 8:19 those that make chirpings and mutterings , of necromancers and wizards.
